events.title: Eastern Market — Weekend Market & Flea
events.description: Historic public market plus weekend outdoor flea, arts, and crafts. Live music when weather permits.

events.title: Capitol Hill Farmers Markets
events.description: Seasonal weekend farmers markets with local produce and vendors.

events.title: Lincoln Park
events.description: Large Capitol Hill green space with playground, paths, and statues. Dog-friendly. Cafes at both ends.

events.title: Garfield Park
events.description: Neighborhood park with playground, tennis, basketball, bocce, and a community garden.

events.title: Yards Park & Navy Yard Waterfront
events.description: Riverfront park with fountains, boardwalk, and frequent seasonal weekend programming.

events.title: National Mall & Smithsonian Museums
events.description: Free Smithsonian museums and monuments. Reliable all-weather, all-ages option.

events.title: United States Botanic Garden
events.description: Free conservatory and gardens at the foot of the Capitol, with a Children's Garden.

events.title: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail Ride
events.description: Paved riverfront trail for a family bike ride, with Capital Bikeshare access nearby.

events.title: The Fields at RFK — Community Open Play & Disc Golf
events.time: Open hours vary (8 AM–dusk disc golf)
events.venue: The Fields at RFK Campus (401 Oklahoma Ave NE)
events.description: Turf fields with community open-play hours plus DC's free disc golf course. 10-min walk from Stadium-Armory.

events.title: CHAW Gallery (Capitol Hill Arts Workshop)
events.venue: Capitol Hill Arts Workshop (545 7th St SE)
events.description: Rotating gallery shows of local artists, two blocks from Eastern Market. Check site for current exhibition.

events.title: Escape with Washington Improv Theater
events.description: WIT's 'Escape with Washington Improv Theater' summer series runs Saturdays at Studio Theatre (1501 14th St NW). Three shows available on Aug 1: 4 PM, 6 PM, and 8 PM. Completely unscripted long-form improv comedy from DC's premier improv company. Pay-what-you-can pricing; door tickets are $20.

events.title: Escape with Washington Improv Theater
events.description: WIT's ongoing Saturday improv series continues at Studio Theatre. Long-form unscripted comedy by DC's most experienced improvisers. Multiple showtimes. Pay-what-you-can; $20 door price.

events.title: TLC – A New Musical (Working Title)
events.venue: Arena Stage (Fichandler Stage), Mead Center for American Theater
events.price: Tickets vary; under-30 and rush pricing typically available at Arena Stage
events.description: Arena Stage's summer 2026 production running through August 9, with confirmed performances on the Aug 1 and Aug 8 weekends. TLC blazed a trail and changed the game — the trio stormed the '90s in this vibrant stage production. Exact production title to confirm on arenastage.org.

events.title: Water Lantern Festival – National Harbor
events.time: Gates open 5:30 PM; Lantern Launch 8:30–9:30 PM
events.venue: National Harbor SouthPointe, 802 National Harbor Blvd, Oxon Hill, MD
events.price: $30.99 General Admission (includes lantern kit, LED candle, markers)
events.description: A two-night water lantern festival at National Harbor. Gates open at 5:30 PM each night with food trucks, music, and fun. Guests design their lanterns starting at 8 PM and launch them on the water from 8:30–9:30 PM. Tickets are high-demand and expected to sell out.

events.title: Escape with Washington Improv Theater
events.description: WIT's 'Escape' series moves to the ground-floor Shargai space at Studio Theatre in the second half of the run. Long-form unscripted improv comedy. Multiple Saturday showtimes. Pay-what-you-can; $20 at door.

events.title: Panda Fest DC 2026
events.time: Sat 10 AM – 10 PM; Sun 10 AM – 8 PM
events.description: Panda Fest makes its DC debut on Pennsylvania Avenue NW, one of the largest outdoor Asian food festivals in the US. Featuring 90+ Asian food vendors, 200+ street food offerings, 40+ merchandise vendors, live cultural performances, panda inflatables and bounce house, and family-friendly activities.

events.title: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness — NMAH Exhibit + DCPL Discovery Day
events.time: Museum hours (free, registration recommended for programming days)
events.venue: National Museum of American History, 1300 Constitution Ave NW
events.description: The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History leads America's 250th anniversary celebrations with this immersive exhibition tracing how Americans have pursued the founding ideals of the Declaration of Independence. DC Public Library partners with the museum for Discover Summer programming days: stop by the DCPL table for activities, suggested reading lists, and library swag. The museum is free; register via DCPL's Discover Summer page for programming day details.

events.title: DCPL Discover Summer — Back-to-School Season-Long Programming
events.description: Throughout August, DC Public Library branches across the District host free back-to-school events featuring bookbag and school supply giveaways, games, crafts, face painting, live entertainment, wellness resources, and more. Families can also sign up for a free library card. The Discover Summer program for teens includes the Know Your Power Teen Art Contest and creative workshops in music, visual arts, and writing. Check individual branch calendars for specific dates and times.

events.title: Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, DC
events.venue: National Mall Street Circuit (1.7-mile loop, Pennsylvania Ave to National Mall)
events.price: Free general admission (GA ticket required; limited paid grandstand seating available)
events.description: The first-ever NTT INDYCAR SERIES race in the nation's capital, marking the US Semiquincentennial. A 1.7-mile, 7-turn street circuit loops the National Mall past the Washington Monument, US Capitol, and Smithsonian museums. Includes practice, qualifying, IROC support race (featuring IndyCar and NASCAR legends), and the main race broadcast live on FOX on Sunday, August 23. Note: the free GA ticket request window has closed; limited paid grandstand options may remain.

events.title: U.S. Navy Band Concerts on the Avenue
events.venue: U.S. Navy Memorial Plaza, Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Free summer evening concerts on the Navy Memorial Plaza. August 18 features the Navy Band Cruisers; August 25 features the full Navy Concert Band. Programs include classical favorites, Broadway hits, and modern chart-toppers celebrating Navy heritage.

events.title: Military Bands Capitol Summer Concert Series
events.venue: U.S. Capitol West Front (National Mall side)
events.description: Free outdoor concerts by U.S. military bands (Navy Band, Air Force Band, Marine Band, Army Band) on the West Front of the U.S. Capitol. No tickets required. Lawn chairs permitted. Runs select evenings July 13 through August 28, 2026.

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend Outdoor Market (Saturday)
events.description: Eastern Market's Saturday outdoor market runs along 7th St SE from Pennsylvania Ave SE to North Carolina Ave SE, featuring local farmers, artisan crafters, prepared food sellers, and live music. Part of the expanded summer season running through September 26.

events.title: Wharf Farmers Market (Saturday)
events.description: Weekly Saturday farmers market at M Street Landing at The Wharf, supporting local farmers offering locally sourced food. Ongoing through the season.

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend Outdoor Market (Sunday)
events.description: Eastern Market's Sunday outdoor flea and farmers market features local farmers, artists, crafters, and prepared food sellers along 7th St SE. Live music often accompanies browsing. Runs through September 27.

events.title: The Notebook – The Musical (National Tour)
events.time: Various (evenings 7:30 PM; matinees on select days)
events.venue: The National Theatre, 1321 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Based on the best-selling novel that inspired the iconic film, The Notebook is a deeply moving portrait of the enduring power of love, presented as part of Broadway at the National's touring season. Runs through the Aug 22 and Aug 29 weekends.

events.title: Sunset Movies at the Wharf
events.description: The Wharf's popular Sunset Movies outdoor film series runs through September 2. Upcoming screenings include '10 Things I Hate About You' on August 12 on Transit Pier at 7:30 PM, presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: Bad Medicine: A Monument to Comedy (Sketch Show)
events.description: Bad Medicine's brand-new hour of sketch comedy takes aim at DC landmarks, political institutions, and cultural icons. Described as 'A Monument to Comedy,' the show satirizes the grandeur and dysfunction of Washington, DC. Playing in the Lounge Showroom at DC Improv.

events.title: Richard O'Brien's The Rocky Horror Show
events.venue: Monumental Theatre Company (venue TBC on atlasarts.org / company site)
events.price: Varies; check TodayTix for rush/lottery pricing
events.description: Monumental Theatre Company's production of the cult classic Rocky Horror Show runs August 22–September 6, 2026, overlapping the Aug 22, Aug 29, and Sep 5 weekends. A celebration of the iconic musical.

events.title: Smithsonian Arts & Industries Building: Voices and Votes – Exploring Democracy Across America
events.venue: Arts and Industries Building, Smithsonian Institution
events.description: In the Smithsonian's second-oldest building next to the Smithsonian Castle, explore what American independence really means and how that meaning has evolved from the American Revolution to today. Part of DC's America 250 celebrations.

events.title: District Vibes / American Pride: How DC Changed American Culture (Exhibition)
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library, 901 G Street NW
events.description: Discover how DC gave the world the football huddle, the modern blood bank, and legends like Marvin Gaye. This exhibit explores the vibrant contributions of Washingtonians through images, artifacts, storytelling and free programs, running through September 27 at the MLK Library with satellite locations across the city.

events.title: Into the Waters with Senju and Bingyi (Exhibition)
events.venue: National Museum of Asian Art, Smithsonian
events.description: Japanese artists Hiroshi Senju and Bingyi and their contrasting visualizations of water — Senju's abstract approach versus Bingyi's traditional methods — form the basis of this hypnotic exhibit at the National Museum of Asian Art, running through September 27.

events.title: America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration — US Botanic Garden
events.venue: United States Botanic Garden Conservatory & Bartholdi Gardens
events.description: In celebration of America's 250th anniversary, the USBG showcases the official flowers of all 50 states, D.C., and U.S. territories via living plants, botanical illustrations, herbarium specimens, and intricate paper flower art by botanical artist Emily Paluska. Visitors can do a self-guided scavenger hunt through the conservatory and outdoor gardens. Drop-in demonstrations and workshops run throughout the exhibit's run. No tickets required.

events.title: Fierce Flora: Tales of Survival and Demise — US Botanic Garden Exhibit
events.description: A walk-through exhibit exploring the unique and sometimes dangerous survival features plants have evolved to defend themselves. Free and open to the public daily. Runs concurrently with the America's State Flowers exhibit.

events.title: ALL THE FEELINGS TOUR: Metric, Broken Social Scene, and Stars
events.description: Triple-bill indie/alt-rock tour featuring Canadian icons Metric, Broken Social Scene, and Stars at The Anthem on the Wharf.

events.title: Marcus D. Wiley – Weekend Headliner
events.description: Marcus D. Wiley headlines the DC Improv in an upcoming weekend run. DC Improv features two showrooms and is downtown near Dupont Circle. All patrons must be 18+ with a 2-item food/beverage minimum.

events.title: Lord Huron
events.description: Indie folk-rock band Lord Huron performing at The Anthem on the DC Wharf.

events.title: Navy Yard Summer Concert Series: Perfekt Blend (Rescheduled)
events.venue: Yards Park Boardwalk (355 Water Street SE)
events.description: Free Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series (14th season) at the Yards Park boardwalk on the Anacostia River. Perfekt Blend — a high-energy DC-based band blending Top 40, Motown, funk, pop, and R&B — was rescheduled here after a July air-quality cancellation. Family-friendly lyrics, grassy open space, food and beverages nearby.

events.title: Rock the Dock Free Concert: Salsa Dance Night with Cubano Groove
events.venue: Transit Pier at The Wharf (970 Wharf Street SW)
events.description: Salsa Dance Night featuring Salsa with Silvia and live music by Cubano Groove. Part of the Rock the Dock free summer concert series on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier, presented by Pacifico Beer. All-ages outdoor pier concert with dancing.

events.title: Chesapeake DockDogs Competition
events.description: Chesapeake DockDogs brings their nationally sanctioned DockDogs competition to District Pier. Cheer on canine athletes as they compete for the title of Iron Dog — the first such event held in DC.

events.title: Community Cooldown at The Fields Pavilion @ RFK
events.venue: The Fields Pavilion @ RFK Campus, 401 Oklahoma Ave NE
events.description: Ward 7 community activation featuring free sweets from Enjoyee Life Ice, JumpDC Superstars performances, and DJ Chan Don. Part of Events DC's Community Cooldown Summer Series bringing free activities to all 8 DC wards.

events.title: Congressional Cemetery Creative Crypt – Chatty Artist Session
events.description: Congressional Cemetery's Creative Crypt series offers artist sessions in two varieties – chatty and silent – to spark creativity whether you work with fabric, writing, or another medium. The next chatty session falls on August 8.

events.title: Dance Nights on Transit Pier at The Wharf
events.description: The Wharf's free themed dance nights combine live music and al fresco cocktails on Transit Pier on select Fridays all summer. Each night features a different style of music and dancing.

events.title: DockDogs Competition at The Wharf
events.description: Chesapeake DockDogs brings their nationally sanctioned DockDogs competition to District Pier for the first time in DC. Cheer on canine athletes as they compete for the title of Iron Dog in high-flying, tail-wagging dock diving action.

events.title: Elefest at the National Zoo — Discover Summer Library Day
events.description: DC Public Library joins the National Zoo's Elephant Day, a celebration of Asian elephants and the Smithsonian's long-standing commitment to their care and conservation. DC librarians host special storytimes, give away DCPL swag, and share recommended titles.

events.title: Mahjong Tournament at Union Market
events.description: Compete or play for fun in a multi-style mahjong tournament at Union Market. Listed in Washingtonian's August Culture Guide.

events.title: WABA Anacostia Scavenger Ride
events.description: Summer scavenger ride with games, surprises, and splashy fun! A free, family-friendly WABA ride starting at the Anacostia Skate Pavilion.

events.title: WABA Family Ride to Peirce Mill
events.description: Bike with WABA instructors to Peirce Mill in Rock Creek Park to learn how ice cream was made before electricity. A family-friendly guided ride departing from Powell Recreation Center.

events.title: Live Concert – The Atlantis (IMP Presents)
events.description: IMP-presented show at The Atlantis on U Street. Artist TBA — tickets on sale; check impconcerts.com for headliner.

events.title: WABA Red Line Corridor Group Ride
events.description: WABA-guided group ride along the Red Line Corridor on Mondays at 8:30 AM through August 31. The route starts at North Bethesda Metro and uses the Trolley Trail and Capital Crescent Trail to visit Medical Center and Bethesda stations, ending at Friendship Heights. A supported alternative to shuttle buses during Red Line construction.

events.title: Sunset Cinema: 10 Things I Hate About You
events.description: Free outdoor screening of the 1999 rom-com classic on The Wharf's Transit Pier LED screen, presented by Pacifico Beer. Chairs open at 7 PM, film at 7:30 PM. All ages welcome; dogs on leash OK. Part of the Wednesday Sunset Cinema series running through September 2.

events.title: Rock the Dock Free Concert: The Experience Band & Show (Go-Go)
events.description: The Experience Band & Show brings DC Go-Go energy to Transit Pier as part of the Rock the Dock free summer concert series, presented by Pacifico Beer. Part of a weekly Friday-night series running May 29 – September 4.

events.title: Rock the Dock Free Concert: The Experience Band & Show (Go-Go)
events.venue: Transit Pier at The Wharf (970 Wharf Street SW)
events.description: The Experience Band & Show performs Go-Go at The Wharf's free Rock the Dock concert series on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier. Go-Go is DC's native music genre. Presented by Pacifico Beer. All-ages outdoor pier show.

events.title: 2nd Annual Back to School Bash — Francis A. Gregory Neighborhood Library
events.venue: Francis A. Gregory Neighborhood Library, 3660 Alabama Ave SE
events.description: A family-friendly back-to-school celebration at the Francis A. Gregory Neighborhood Library featuring music, moon bounces, a petting zoo, face painting, and free school supplies for students. Presented by DC Public Library.

events.title: DC Power FC vs. Carolina Ascent – Season Opener
events.description: DC Power FC's season opener at Audi Field takes on the Carolina Ascent. Mentioned as a standout local event in The Hill is Home's late-July To Do List.

events.title: Live Concert – 9:30 Club (IMP Presents)
events.description: IMP-presented show at 9:30 Club on Saturday August 15. Artist TBA — tickets available; check 930.com for headliner.

events.title: Takoma Streets Ride with Takoma Family Biking
events.venue: Takoma Park Streatery, 6909 Laurel Ave NW, Takoma Park, MD
events.description: Join Takoma Family Biking for a 3-mile neighborhood streets ride launching at 2 PM from the Takoma Park Streatery. Hosted in partnership with WABA. Great for families and newer riders.

events.title: Back to School Festival — Woodridge Neighborhood Library
events.venue: Woodridge Neighborhood Library, 1801 Hamlin Street NE
events.description: Annual Back to School Festival at Woodridge Library, a free afternoon of family fun featuring live entertainment and back-to-school resources. Part of DCPL's August back-to-school programming series.

events.title: U.S. Marine Band Summer Concert at Yards Park
events.description: The President's Own United States Marine Band performs a free outdoor concert on the Yards Park boardwalk, with views of the Anacostia River. Bring a picnic blanket.

events.title: DC Bike Party – August
events.description: Monthly social community bike ride around Washington, DC. DC Bike Party is a leaderless gathering of bike and city-life enthusiasts. The August edition typically runs ~6 miles over ~75 minutes, departing the Dupont Circle fountain around 7:30 PM. Check organizer social channels for same-day confirmation.

events.title: Sunset Cinema: F1 (2025)
events.description: Free outdoor screening of the 2025 Formula 1 racing film on The Wharf's Transit Pier, presented by Pacifico Beer. Chairs open at 7 PM, film at 7:30 PM. All ages welcome; dogs on leash OK.

events.title: Rock Creek Kings at The Wharf Floating Stage
events.venue: Transit Pier Floating Stage, The Wharf
events.description: Rock Creek Kings bring their versatile sound of pop, rock, and folk to the Floating Stage at Transit Pier on Friday, August 21 as part of The Wharf's summer music series.

events.title: Rock the Dock Free Concert: Rock Creek Kings (Rock)
events.description: Rock Creek Kings perform pop, rock, and folk on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier. Part of the Rock the Dock free summer concert series, presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: Celebrate Holland Lane Bike Lanes with BPAC & WABA (Alexandria Ride + Social)
events.description: Take a spin on Alexandria's newest bike lanes (Holland Lane) then gather with bike advocates for an end-of-summer social at Atlas Brew Works. Co-hosted by WABA and the Alexandria Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee (BPAC).

events.title: Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. — IndyCar on the National Mall
events.description: The first-ever NTT IndyCar Series race on the National Mall, part of America's 250th anniversary celebrations. The Freedom 250 Grand Prix runs August 22–23, 2026. Note: This event also caused the USBG to reschedule its August Summer Evening Hours from Aug 21 to Aug 27.

events.title: Jay Pharoah – Weekend Headliner
events.description: Jay Pharoah, known for his run on Saturday Night Live and unmatched celebrity impressions, headlines the DC Improv for a second weekend engagement. Multiple shows Friday–Sunday. 18+ with 2-item minimum.

events.title: Library of Congress National Book Festival 2026
events.venue: Walter E. Washington Convention Center, 801 Allen Y. Lew Place NW
events.description: The 26th annual Library of Congress National Book Festival, free and open to the public at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center. Features author talks, programming for all ages, and a selection of programs livestreamed online. Free tickets are required for entry. Near Mount Vernon Square Metro (Yellow/Green lines).

events.title: Pints for Paws with Pacifico
events.price: Free to attend; drinks for purchase
events.description: Dog-friendly afternoon happy hour on Transit Pier. Bring your pup, grab a Pacifico from Cantina Bambina, and enjoy waterfront views. Proceeds benefit local animal shelters. Special tennis ball engraving for dogs available on select dates.

events.title: Story Time with DC Public Library at the National Museum of Natural History
events.venue: National Museum of Natural History, 1300 Constitution Ave NW
events.ageRestriction: Designed for ages 5 and under; all welcome
events.description: Monthly Story Time co-hosted by the National Museum of Natural History and DC Public Library. Children and their grown-ups enjoy a story designed to explore language and literacy skills. Primarily designed for learners ages 5 and under, though all are welcome.

events.title: Sunset Cinema: Project Hail Mary
events.description: Free outdoor screening of the 2026 sci-fi film Project Hail Mary on The Wharf's Transit Pier, presented by Pacifico Beer. All ages welcome; dogs on leash OK.

events.title: USBG Summer Evening Hours with Live Music (Breonna Sharde')
events.description: The USBG's rescheduled August Summer Evening Hours (moved from the original third Thursday due to the Freedom 250 Grand Prix). The Garden stays open until 8 PM for golden-hour exploration of the America's State Flowers exhibit alongside live music from Breonna Sharde', blending soul, jazz, and bossa nova with a hint of disco. Botanical mocktails and snacks available for purchase from Vintage Views. Note: This falls just outside the target weekends (Thursday, Aug 27) but is worth noting for families.

events.title: Chxrry
events.description: Chxrry performs at Pearl Street Warehouse on the Friday night of the Aug 29 weekend. 21+ venue.

events.title: Rock the Dock Free Concert: Secret Society (Go-Go & Jazz)
events.description: Secret Society brings Go-Go and Jazz to Transit Pier as part of the Rock the Dock free summer concert series, presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: LaVar Walker – Stand-Up Comedy
events.description: LaVar Walker, an American stand-up comedian, writer, and pharmacist who has appeared on television and toured nationally, headlines Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse. 7 PM show. 21+ unless with a parent. 2903 Columbia Pike, Arlington, VA.

events.title: Pump Action
events.description: Pump Action plays Pearl Street Warehouse. Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm. 21+ venue per venue policy.

events.title: Social Distortion with Descendents and The Chats
events.description: Punk rock triple-bill: Social Distortion headlining with support from Descendents and The Chats at The Anthem. Friday of the Sep 5 weekend.

events.title: Nick Thune – Stand-Up Comedy
events.description: Nick Thune, actor/comedian/writer known for his deadpan delivery and absurdist storytelling, headlines Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse. 7 PM show. 21+ unless with a parent. 2903 Columbia Pike, Arlington, VA.

events.title: Pete Correale – DC Improv Headlining Debut
events.description: Pete Correale, co-host of The Pete and Sebastian Show and veteran of The Tonight Show, Letterman, and Conan, makes his DC Improv headlining debut this fall. Multiple shows over the weekend. 18+ with 2-item minimum.
